facts.value: Threskeia was loosely translated into Latin as religiō in late antiquity.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies Degree — Bachelor of Arts

facts.value: Threskeia was sparsely used in classical Greece.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies Degree — Bachelor of Arts

facts.value: It became more frequently used in the writings of Josephus in the 1st century CE.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies Degree — Bachelor of Arts

facts.value: Threskeia could mean multiple things from respectful fear to excessive or harmfully distracting practices of others, to cultic practices.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies Degree — Bachelor of Arts

facts.value: It was often contrasted with the Greek word deisidaimonia, which meant too much fear.
facts.programme_association: Religious Studies Degree — Bachelor of Arts
